cards.title: 4.1 What is a Muscle
body: **A muscle** is a body structure that is made up of fibrous tissue.
A complete muscle contains bundles of muscle fibres.
Muscle tissue is highly specialized to contract or shorten forcefully.
Muscle fibres become shorter during contraction and if the muscle tissue is attached to a bone, joint movement will result.
Together, the skeletal and muscular systems support the body and allow movement.

cards.title: Worked from review
cards.problem: Which of the following muscle tissues is characterized by being striated, branched, and containing intercalated discs?

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze tissue structural features**
Striations are present in both skeletal and cardiac muscles.
Branched fibers and intercalated discs, however, are exclusive structural features of cardiac muscle cells.
**Step 2: Compare options**
Skeletal muscle is unbranched and multinucleated.

cards.title: Worked from review
cards.problem: Skeletal muscle fibers are multinucleated. This anatomical feature is a developmental result of which of the following processes?

steps.text: **Step 1: Review muscle embryology**
Skeletal muscle fibers are giant cells that contain hundreds of nuclei located just beneath the cell membrane.
**Step 2: Identify developmental origin**
During embryonic development, multiple individual cells called myoblasts fuse together end-to-end to form a single long muscle fiber, combining their nuclei.
**Step 3: Final Result**

cards.answer: The fusion of multiple embryonic myoblast cells

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following statements regarding smooth muscle tissue is correct?

options.A: It is striated and under conscious voluntary control.
options.B: It is composed of spindle-shaped cells, lacks striations, and is involuntary.
options.C: It is multinucleated and located exclusively in the heart.
options.D: It contracts rapidly and fatigues very easily.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Evaluate smooth muscle anatomy**
Smooth muscle cells are fusiform (spindle-shaped) with a single central nucleus and lack repeating sarcomeres, making them non-striated.

**Step 2: Evaluate control and function**
Smooth muscle is involuntary, contracting slowly and staying contracted for long periods without fatiguing.

**Step 3: Final Result**
Therefore, the correct choice is **It is composed of spindle-shaped cells, lacks striations, and is involuntary.**

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What connects a skeletal muscle belly directly to the bone, transmitting the force of contraction?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Distinguish musculoskeletal connective tissues**
Ligaments connect bone to bone. Fascia surrounds muscles. The sarcolemma is the muscle cell membrane.

**Step 2: Identify force transmitter**
A tendon is a dense band of fibrous regular connective tissue that connects the muscle belly directly to the bone, transmitting force.

**Step 3: Final Result**
Therefore, the correct choice is **Tendon**.

cards.title: Muscles: fuller notes
body: Together, the skeletal and muscular systems support the body and allow movement. A tendon attaches muscle to bone.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The function of a tendon is to

options.D: bind the cells in compact bone closer together.

cards.why: A **tendon** is a fibrous connective tissue that attaches **muscle to bone**. This allows the force of muscle contraction to move the skeleton.

cards.title: Voluntary Muscles
body: Muscles only *pull*. So they work in pairs: biceps flexes the elbow, triceps extends it. Origin = anchor; insertion = the bone that moves.

cards.title: 4.2.1 Muscles and Bones
body: **A skeletal muscle** is an organ of the muscular system.
An individual skeletal muscle is separated from adjacent muscles and held in position by layers of fibrous connective tissue.
**The tendon** is a structure that attaches muscle to bone.
The skeletal bones move only when the muscles attached to them contract, thus pulling the muscle towards the point of origin.

cards.title: 4.2.2 Action of Voluntary Muscles
body: Skeletal muscles almost always function in groups (or pairs).
When a particular body part moves, it must do more than contract a single muscle.
Muscles are usually paired, producing movement in opposite directions.
One muscle contracts while the other is relaxed.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following muscle tissues is characterized by being striated, branched, and containing intercalated discs?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze tissue structural features**
Striations are present in both skeletal and cardiac muscles. Branched fibers and intercalated discs, however, are exclusive structural features of cardiac muscle cells.

**Step 2: Compare options**

**Step 3: Final Result**
Therefore, the correct choice is **Cardiac muscle**.

cards.title: Antagonistic pair: biceps and triceps
body: To bend the arm the biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes. To straighten it the triceps contracts and the biceps relaxes.

cards.title: Worked example: lifting a load
cards.problem: A student lifts a book by bending the elbow. Describe what each muscle does.

steps.text: The biceps contracts and pulls the forearm up.
The triceps relaxes.
To lower the book, the triceps contracts while the biceps gradually relaxes.

cards.answer: Biceps contracts to bend; triceps contracts to straighten.

steps.text: Muscle to bone.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Movement of bones in two directions is done by __________ of muscles.
cards.why: Muscles can only pull, not push. To move a bone in two directions (e.g., bending and straightening an arm), muscles must work in **antagonistic pairs** (like biceps and triceps), where one contracts while the other relaxes.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The movable and immovable ends of a muscle are ____and____respectively.
cards.why: In anatomy, the **origin** is the attachment site that doesn't move during contraction, while the **insertion** is the attachment site that does move when the muscle contracts.

cards.title: 4.3.1 Smooth Muscles
body: Smooth muscle tissue is so named because their cells lack striations.
Smooth muscles are located in the walls of the hollow organs, blood vessels, eyes, glands and skin.
The walls of the stomach, intestines, urinary bladder and uterus are formed by smooth muscle tissue.

cards.title: 4.3.2 Cardiac Muscles
body: The resulting muscle fibres are branched and interconnected in complex networks.
Cardiac muscle, like smooth muscle, is controlled automatically.
Cardiac muscle has the capacity to contract and relax rhythmically throughout life without becoming fatigued.
The cardiac muscles are auto-rhythmic and a node of the heart acts as the pacemaker.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The site of attachment of a muscle to a relatively stationary or fixed bone is called the:
cards.why:
**Step 1: Review muscle attachment definitions**
Skeletal muscles have an origin, a belly, and an insertion.

**Step 2: Match with stationary site**
The origin is the site of attachment to the stationary or less mobile bone. The insertion is the attachment to the mobile bone.

**Step 3: Final Result**
Therefore, the correct choice is **Origin**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following describes the relationship between the biceps brachii and triceps brachii during forearm flexion?

options.A: Both muscles contract simultaneously as synergists.
options.B: The biceps brachii acts as the agonist (flexor) while the triceps brachii acts as the antagonist (extensor) and relaxes.
options.C: The triceps brachii acts as the agonist while the biceps brachii relaxes.
options.D: Both muscles relax completely under somatic inhibition.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze forearm flexion mechanics**
Bending the arm at the elbow joint is flexion, which decreases the joint angle.

**Step 2: Map to agonist and antagonist roles**
The biceps brachii is the flexor (agonist) and contracts. The triceps brachii is the extensor (antagonist) and must relax and stretch.

**Step 3: Final Result**
Therefore, the correct choice is **The biceps brachii acts as the agonist (flexor) while the triceps brachii acts as the antagonist (extensor) and relaxes.**

cards.q: Peristalsis in the alimentary canal is produced by ____.

options.D: smooth (involuntary) muscle in the gut wall

cards.why:
**Step 1:** The gut wall has circular and longitudinal layers of smooth muscle.

**Step 2:** Their waves of contraction push food along.

**Step 3:** This is involuntary – we do not control it consciously.

glossary.meaning: A skeletal muscle is an organ of the muscular system.
The tendon is a structure that attaches muscle to bone.

tips.text: A muscle is made up of fibrous tissue that is able to contract and relax.
Bones are able to move around a joint, due to the contraction and relaxation of muscles, which causes movement in the skeletal system.

The activity of muscles is co-ordinated by the nervous system. There are three types of muscles in the human body: skeletal muscle, also called voluntary muscle; cardiac muscle; and smooth muscle, also called involuntary muscle.
The majority of skeletal muscles are paired and produce movement in the opposite direction across skeletal joints i.e. when one muscle contracts, the other relaxes, by way of antagonistic action.
Involuntary muscles are those muscles that are not controlled by will.
Unlike skeletal muscle, both smooth and cardiac muscles are involuntary muscles.
Smooth muscles control the involuntary activities of the body.
Cardiac muscle tissue is found only in the heart. This muscle continues its activities without being stimulated by nerve impulses.

cards.back: Contractile fibres shorten. To lengthen, the antagonist must contract (or gravity helps). That is the whole lever story of Unit 3 + 4 together.

questions.q: Which of the following muscle type is closely associated to visceral organs?
why:
**Logic:**
- **Skeletal muscle:** Attached to bones (striated, voluntary).
- **Smooth muscle:** Found in the walls of internal (**visceral**) organs like the stomach, intestines, and blood vessels. It is non-striated and involuntary.
- **Cardiac muscle:** Found only in the heart.

**Result:**
Smooth muscle.

similar.q: How is the oxygen debt repaid?
similar.a: By deep breathing after exercise to oxidise the lactic acid.

similar.q: Which respiration releases more energy, aerobic or anaerobic?

questions.answer: Lactic acid builds up because of anaerobic respiration when oxygen supply is too low.
why: During hard exercise muscles need more energy than oxygen can supply.
They respire anaerobically: glucose → lactic acid.
Lactic acid builds up, causing fatigue and cramp (an oxygen debt).
